answer.recommendation:
Draft customer FAQ for Scheduled Exports (launches November 4)

Q: What is scheduled exports?
A: It lets you set up exports of your data to run on a schedule, delivered in CSV or JSON format.

Q: Is scheduled export real-time?
A: No. Scheduled exports run on a schedule and are not real-time synchronization. Changes made between runs will not appear until the next export runs.

Q: What file formats are supported?
A: CSV and JSON.

Q: How many rows can one export include?
A: Up to 10,000 rows per export.

Q: What happens if my data exceeds 10,000 rows?
A: [OPEN ITEM - to be confirmed by product team before publishing: whether the export is truncated, fails with an error, or is split into multiple files.]

Q: How often can exports run, and how long are files kept?
A: [OPEN ITEM - schedule frequency options, file retention period, and time zone behavior are not in the work packet and must be confirmed before publishing.]

Quality notes on this draft: The work packet supplies only formats, the row limit, and the launch date. Colleagues C1, C2, and C4 did not provide confirmation of overflow behavior, schedule frequency, or retention; C2 and C4 said they had no additional task-specific information. The real-time misconception comes from C1's reply. Do not publish the FAQ until the open items are answered by the feature owner.
quality_notes: baseline_summary is copied exactly from the supplied work packet.
Overflow behavior above 10,000 rows is unconfirmed; the FAQ marks it as an open item rather than guessing.
Schedule frequency, retention, and time zone limits are not in the packet and were not confirmed by colleagues; marked as open items.
The 'not real-time' point is sourced from C1's reply (sales engineer's observation about customer confusion).
C2 and C4 reported no additional task-specific information; C3 was not contacted because the other colleagues did not hold the needed facts and C3's profile is general coordination.
Recommend the feature owner confirm open items before the November 4 launch.
